title: Pool and Spa Service Software (2026): 5 Tools Compared
description: Pool and spa service software compared: which tools track spas as separate bodies of water, spa-specific features, and what a pool-and-spa route costs.
h1: Pool and spa service software: spas, hot tubs and multiple bodies of water compared
body:
Plenty of pool routes include a spa or hot tub at the same address, and some service companies look after spas on their own: drain-and-refills, filter cleans and repairs. This page compares five tools on how they handle a property with more than one body of water: whether a spa gets its own record, readings and equipment, how it changes your bill, and what that costs. Every fact comes from the vendors' own pricing and feature pages, checked 2026-11-27. Anything a vendor doesn't publish is marked unknown, and we say when a vendor doesn't mention spas by name. For overall picks see best pool service software; for chemical logs and service reports see pool maintenance software; and for every pool tool we track, the pool service hub.

What a pool-and-spa route costs on each tool

Two example routes where every address has a pool and a spa, so there are twice as many bodies of water as addresses. These are monthly list prices worked out from each vendor's published formula, before add-ons, taxes and payment processing.

ToolSolo: 40 addresses (80 bodies of water), 1 techSmall crew: 80 addresses (160 bodies of water), 2 techs
Skimmer$49/mo (Getting Started covers up to 49 serviced locations; Getting Started is listed for businesses servicing 0 to 49 pools a month)$160/mo on Scaling Up ($98 base including 49 locations + 31 × $2), the plan listed for 50 to 1,000 pools a month
UpBuoy$120/mo on Professional (40 × $3; above the $99 minimum). The free Essential plan stops at 3 locations$240/mo (80 × $3)
Pool Brain$115/mo ($50 + $65)$180/mo ($50 + 2 × $65)
Pool Office Manager$125/mo$150/mo ($125 + $25)
Jobber$29/mo billed annually or $49/mo monthly (Core). Route optimization isn't on Core$58/mo billed annually (Core $29 + one $29 user), or Connect from $99/mo billed annually for 1 user plus $29/mo per added user if you need route optimization

None of the five publishes a charge per extra body of water, so adding the spa at an address you already service doesn't raise the software bill on any of them. Skimmer and UpBuoy count each address once a month however many bodies of water it has; Pool Brain, Pool Office Manager and Jobber don't charge per pool at all. What a spa does change is the work: a second set of readings, its own dosing and its own equipment list. That's where per-body-of-water records matter.

How to choose software for pool and spa service

  • Spa-only or spa-heavy business: UpBuoy is the only one of the five with a page built for spa and hot tub service, listing drain/refill service types and spa equipment by year, make and model.
  • Pool routes where some homes also have a spa: Skimmer bills per address, not per body of water. Pool Brain and Pool Office Manager don't charge per pool and keep a separate record for each body of water.
  • Accurate dosing for a small spa: Pool Office Manager says its dosing uses each body of water's actual gallons. Pool Brain auto-calculates dosing from readings. Skimmer's Orenda LSI & dosing calculator is on Scaling Up, not Getting Started.
  • Charging a different price for the spa: Pool Brain lists pricing by body of water. For the other four, confirm in a trial how you'd add a spa line to the recurring invoice.
  • Mixed trades: If you also do lawn, pest or window work, Jobber covers every trade, but its pool page doesn't describe separate bodies of water. Test a pool-plus-spa customer in the trial first.
  • Test it on a real customer. Set up one address with a pool and a spa during the trial and run a visit. Our software buying checklist lists what else to test.

faq: Does pool service software charge extra for a spa?

None of the five tools we compared publishes a per-spa charge. Skimmer bills $1 or $2 per serviced location per month regardless of how many bodies of water are at the address, and its FAQ names pools, spas and fountains. UpBuoy counts each unique address once a month ($3/location on Professional). Pool Brain ($50/mo + $65 per tech), Pool Office Manager ($125/mo + $25 per extra user) and Jobber (per user) don't charge per pool (checked 2026-11-27).
Which software is built for spa and hot tub service?

Of the tools we track, UpBuoy is the only one with a dedicated spa cleaning page. It lists spa equipment tracking by year, make and model, drain/refill, maintenance and repair service types, card-on-file billing and spa supply inventory (checked 2026-11-27).
Can I log separate readings for the pool and the spa?

Skimmer tracks readings and service history across multiple bodies of water. Pool Brain tracks chemical use, equipment and workflow by body of water. Pool Office Manager keeps each body of water's reading and dosing history and doses from its actual gallons. Jobber's pool page describes checklists for readings but not separate bodies of water, so test that in a trial.
What does pool and spa service software cost for a solo tech?

For 40 addresses with one tech, from each vendor's published formula: Skimmer $49/mo, Pool Brain $115/mo, UpBuoy $120/mo, Pool Office Manager $125/mo, and Jobber Core $29/mo billed annually ($49 monthly) without route optimization. Prices checked 2026-11-27, before add-ons and payment fees.
Is there free pool and spa service software?

UpBuoy's Essential plan is free for up to 3 locations, which is only enough to test it. The other four are paid; Skimmer offers a 30-day refund guarantee and Pool Office Manager a 30-day free trial. See our free pool service software page for more options.
